unit.bounded_unit: Bounded scalar form shr.b32 d, a, b; with optional guard {none, @p, @!p} and bounded machine state value/predicate partial lookups.
unit.scope_boundary: Only the `.b32` type form and 3-operand shape are modeled. Source operands are `SourceOperand.reg` or `SourceOperand.imm` by bounded design; predicates are optional and no memory/special-register/global state is modeled. No explicit error/exception/undefined/implementation-defined behavior is added; partial execution is represented via `Option` in executable semantics and malformed constructor in relation.

theorem_obligations.intent: Prove that `ShrB32Step` yields at most one result state for fixed pre-state and instruction. This is meaningful because semantics are represented as a relation with explicit `guardFalse`, `executed`, and `malformed` constructors.
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: For every state s and instruction i, if `ShrB32Step s i s1` and `ShrB32Step s i s2`, then `s1 = s2`.
theorem_obligations.lean_statement_sketch:
theorem shrB32Step_deterministic
  (s : MachineState) (i : ShrB32Instruction) (s1 s2 : MachineState)
  (h1 : ShrB32Step s i s1) (h2 : ShrB32Step s i s2) : s1 = s2
theorem_obligations.source_or_assumption_basis: Bounded semantics distinguishes three execution-shape constructors and fixed-state transition definitions in `ShrB32-v2.lean`; no preconditions are added beyond the two relation hypotheses.
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: The relation has distinct constructors (`executed`, `guardFalse`, `malformed`), and source/guard branches are nontrivial due to partial reads; the conclusion is not an assumption and rules out distinct successful post-states under one constructor set.
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: Case-split on `h1` and `h2`. Constructor mismatches contradict evalGuard or source-read premises. Matching branches reduce to definitional equality of record updates via same guarded/sourced branch evidence.

theorem_obligations.intent: Relate executable semantics and relation: (a) executed and (b) guard-false and (c) malformed outcomes imply corresponding relation steps, (d) every relation step is produced by some executable outcome, and (e) `execShrB32 s i = none` iff no relation step exists. This captures partial-state behavior as a contract and the newly explicit malformed path.
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: (a) `execShrB32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.executed s') -> ShrB32Step s i s'`; (b) function `guardFalse` outcome implies corresponding relation; (c) function `malformed` outcome implies relation to unchanged state; (d) from `ShrB32Step s i s'` infer existence of matching function outcome; (e) `execShrB32 s i = none` iff no `ShrB32Step s i _` exists.
theorem_obligations.lean_statement_sketch:
theorem execShrB32_sound_executed ...
  (s : MachineState) (i : ShrB32Instruction) (s' : MachineState) (h : execShrB32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.executed s')) : ShrB32Step s i s'

theorem execShrB32_sound_guardFalse ...

theorem execShrB32_sound_malformed ...

theorem shrB32Step_complete ... : ∃ o, execShrB32 s i = some o ∧ (o = ExecOutcome.executed s' ∨ o = ExecOutcome.guardFalse s' ∨ o = ExecOutcome.malformed s')

theorem execShrB32_none_iff_no_step (s i) : execShrB32 s i = none ↔ ¬∃ s', ShrB32Step s i s'
hypotheses: h : execShrB32 s i = some o (for soundness lemmas)
theorem_obligations.conclusion: Four-part equivalence between executable outcomes (`executed`, `guardFalse`, `malformed`, and `none`) and relation availability.
theorem_obligations.source_or_assumption_basis: Relational/executable split is an architecture-approved design choice for this unit; semantics and comments mark malformed as partial-state condition (`none` in function). No invented trap/exception path is introduced.
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: The theorem is essential because relation and function are different shapes: relation is partial and has explicit constructors, while executable is an Option-returning function. The correspondence requires proving both directions, especially that malformed/no-state states are represented consistently.
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: Unfold both definitions and split on `evalGuard`; then split on source lookups. Forward parts follow matching branch constructors. Reverse direction constructs the matching outcome by cases on `ShrB32Step` constructor. For `none` equivalence, use contradiction in both directions from branch coverage in `execShrB32`.

theorem_obligations.intent: Show that, on true guard and resolvable operands, destination write equals the bounded `shrB32Value` result, i.e. right shift by clamped amount (`Nat.min b 32`) with zero-fill semantics for `.b32`.
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: If `evalGuard s i.guard = some true`, `i.d = Destination.reg r`, `readSource s i.a = some va`, `readSource s i.b = some vb`, then there exists `s'` such that `execShrB32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.executed s')` and `s'.valueRegs r = some (shrB32Value va vb)`.
theorem_obligations.lean_statement_sketch:
theorem execShrB32_shr_fidelity (s : MachineState) (i : ShrB32Instruction) (r : RegId) (va vb : B32)
    (hguard : evalGuard s i.guard = some true)
    (hd : i.d = Destination.reg r)
    (ha : readSource s i.a = some va)
    (hb : readSource s i.b = some vb) :
    ∃ s' : MachineState, execShrB32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.executed s') /\ s'.valueRegs r = some (shrB32Value va vb)
hypotheses: hguard : evalGuard s i.guard = some true
ha : readSource s i.a = some va
hb : readSource s i.b = some vb
theorem_obligations.conclusion: When both sources are resolved and guard is true, the computed destination value is exactly `shrB32Value va vb` in the post-state for register destination r.
theorem_obligations.source_or_assumption_basis: Semantics `d = a >> b` plus clamp rule and `.b32` zero-fill behavior are encoded as `shrB32Value`. The theorem also uses the pre-state-source reading and destination-register constructor semantics.
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: The hypothesis provides no concluded destination value; the conclusion pins the exact shifted result and read-before-write behavior, distinguishing it from copy/no-op/wrong-fill alternatives.
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: Unfold `execShrB32` and `shrB32Value`; simplify updateDestination at `i.d = Destination.reg r`; rewrite by `ha`, `hb`, and hguard to force the executed branch. Conclude equality at key by simp.
strength_risks: The statement is bounded to `.b32` zero-fill behavior; signed-fill claims are not asserted for this bounded unit.
`clampShiftAmount` uses the design-dependent binding N=32 for shr.b32; this is an explicit bounded-design dependency (DD-3).

theorem_obligations.intent: Show that execution updates only destination register state in the bounded model and leaves all predicates unchanged, in both executed and guard-false/malformed outcomes when applicable via relation constructors.
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: For any `ShrB32Step s i s'` with `i.d = Destination.reg r`, every predicate register is unchanged and every value register except possibly r is unchanged between s and s'.
theorem_obligations.lean_statement_sketch:
theorem shrB32Step_destination_only_frame
  (s : MachineState) (i : ShrB32Instruction) (s' : MachineState) (r : RegId)
  (hstep : ShrB32Step s i s') (hd : i.d = Destination.reg r) :
  (∀ r' : RegId, r' ≠ r -> s'.valueRegs r' = s.valueRegs r') /\ (∀ p : PredId, s'.predRegs p = s.predRegs p)
theorem_obligations.conclusion: Frame condition: destination is the only possibly updated value register and predicate file is untouched.
theorem_obligations.source_or_assumption_basis: Approved bounded state model only includes value/predicate registers and update code in `updateDestination` changes value-reg map only for one destination register branch.
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: Executed and guard-false/malformed relations are distinct in semantics; this theorem ensures write locality in the executed case and no writes in unchanged-state cases.
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: Split on hstep. Guard-false/malformed constructors reduce to reflexive state equality. Executed constructor reduces by unfolding `updateDestination`; use by_cases on destination equality to show frame for other regs and predRegs unchanged since only valueRegs field is changed.
strength_risks: The claim is over the bounded machine-state only; absent components (memory/status) are intentionally out of scope.
Malformed is treated as no destination update in relation/executable mapping by design of `ShrB32-v2` (stays in-bounds via explicit constructor).

theorem_obligations.intent: Establish the no-op semantics of false guards: if the complete predicate is false, execution returns `ExecOutcome.guardFalse s` and relation reaches state s. This also checks that source reads are not required by the theorem statement.
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: If `evalGuard s i.guard = some false`, then `execShrB32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.guardFalse s)`. Also, if `ShrB32Step s i s'` and `evalGuard s i.guard = some false`, then `s' = s`.
theorem_obligations.lean_statement_sketch:
theorem execShrB32_guard_false_preserves_state (s : MachineState) (i : ShrB32Instruction)
  (hguard : evalGuard s i.guard = some false) :
  execShrB32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.guardFalse s)

theorem shrB32Step_guard_false_frame (s : MachineState) (i : ShrB32Instruction) (s' : MachineState)
  (hstep : ShrB32Step s i s') (hguard : evalGuard s i.guard = some false) : s' = s
hypotheses: hguard : evalGuard s i.guard = some false
theorem_obligations.conclusion: False guard preserves state in both executable and relational forms.
theorem_obligations.source_or_assumption_basis: Predication false-do-nothing semantics are derived from shared control-flow clause for all PTX instructions and the bounded executable/relational shape in `ShrB32-v2.lean`.
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: This does not merely state a tautology of the constructor definition; it confirms that the state carried by `guardFalse` is exactly the unchanged pre-state and that relation branches cannot hide predicate-false execution effects.
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: Forward direction: unfold `execShrB32` and apply hguard. Backward direction: case on hstep; only `guardFalse` branch is compatible with hguard, yielding s' = s by constructor equality.
strength_risks: Ensure theorem does not overclaim do-nothing for components not present in bounded `MachineState`.
